abandoned.ex: They abandoned the plan after the costs rose.

across.es: en todo; a lo largo de

action.en: steps taken by workers, such as a strike
action.ex: The nurses voted for industrial action last month.
action.zh: 行動（industrial action：勞工抗爭、罷工）

afternoon.en: the time between midday and evening
afternoon.ex: We usually go for a walk in the afternoon.

again.ex: The team lost again on Saturday.

agree.en: to have the same opinion; reach a deal
agree.ex: Both sides finally agreed on a new deal.

agreed.ex: The teachers agreed to change the timetable.

agreement.ex: The two companies signed a new agreement.

aim.ex: Her aim is to finish the course this year.

allocated.ex: The council allocated money for new parks.

example.en: The city allocated more money to public transport.
example.zh: 市政府撥了更多經費給大眾運輸。

note.meaning: 把資金、資源或時間正式分配給特定用途。
note.usage: 常用 allocate sth for/to sth；被動 be allocated 很常見，多用於預算與資源的正式語境。

noteEn.meaning: to officially give money, time or resources for a purpose.
noteEn.usage: Use "allocate something to/for something"; the passive "be allocated" is common with budgets.

noteEs.exampleTr: La ciudad asignó más dinero al transporte público.
noteEs.meaning: asignar oficialmente dinero, recursos o tiempo a un fin concreto.
noteEs.usage: Se usa allocate sth to/for sth; la pasiva be allocated es frecuente al hablar de presupuestos.

noteHi.exampleTr: शहर ने सार्वजनिक परिवहन के लिए और पैसे आवंटित किए।
noteHi.meaning: पैसे, संसाधन या समय को किसी खास काम के लिए आधिकारिक रूप से देना।
noteHi.usage: allocate sth to/for sth; passive be allocated बजट के संदर्भ में आम है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 市は公共交通機関により多くの予算を割り当てた。
noteJa.meaning: 資金・資源・時間を特定の目的に正式に割り当てること。
noteJa.usage: allocate A to/for B の形が多い。予算の話では受動態 be allocated がよく使われる。

noteKo.exampleTr: 시는 대중교통에 더 많은 예산을 배정했다.
noteKo.meaning: 돈, 자원, 시간을 특정 용도에 공식적으로 배정하는 것.
noteKo.usage: allocate A to/for B 형태로 쓰며, 예산 관련 글에서 수동태 be allocated가 흔하다.

announced.ex: The school announced a new head teacher.

announcement.ex: The airline made an announcement about the delay.

appointed.en: chose someone officially for a job
appointed.ex: The school appointed a new head teacher.

appointees.en: people chosen officially for a job
appointees.ex: All the new appointees start work next month.

argue.en: to give reasons for an opinion
argue.ex: Critics argue that the plan is too expensive.

aside.en: to one side (set aside: keep for a purpose)
aside.ex: She set aside some money every month.

at.en: used for a place or time; (at once) immediately

attempt.ex: His first attempt at baking was a disaster.

auspices.en: support and control of an organisation
auspices.ex: The event was held under the auspices of the UN.
auspices.zh: 主持（under the auspices of：在…主持下）

averted.ex: Quick action averted a serious accident.

avoid.ex: Try to avoid driving during rush hour.

away.ex: Call the doctor straight away if the pain gets worse.

back-channel.en: secret and unofficial, not through normal routes
back-channel.ex: The two countries held back-channel talks for months.

basis.en: the starting point something is built on
basis.ex: These figures form the basis of our report.

be.en: exist or have a quality; used to form the passive
be.ex: The shop will be open tomorrow.

been.ex: It has been a busy week.

before.ex: I had seen him two days before.

behind-the-scenes.ex: Much behind-the-scenes work goes into every show.

between.en: in the space or time separating two things

big.ex: Moving abroad is a big decision.

blend.ex: The song is a blend of jazz and pop.

body.ex: An independent body will check the election.
body.zh: 機構；團體（umbrella body：聯合總會）

break.ex: The peace talks broke down after two days.

breakthrough.en: an important step forward after difficulty
breakthrough.ex: Scientists made a breakthrough in cancer research.

bring.en: to add or provide something to a group
bring.ex: She brings years of experience to the team.

budget.ex: The government announced its budget on Tuesday.

called.ex: They called off the match because of snow.

came.ex: The good news came after weeks of waiting.

camps.en: groups with the same views in a dispute
camps.ex: The party is split into two camps.

cancelled.ex: The concert was cancelled because of rain.

centres.ex: The debate centres on the cost of housing.

chair.en: the person in charge of a meeting or committee
chair.ex: She was elected chair of the board.

chairperson.en: the person who leads a meeting or group
chairperson.ex: The chairperson opened the meeting at ten.

chairs.en: leads a committee or meeting as its chair
chairs.ex: She chairs the school parents’ committee.

climbdown.en: giving up a position you strongly held
climbdown.ex: The new tax rule was a humiliating climbdown for ministers.

commence.ex: The course will commence in September.

commission.en: an official group with special powers
commission.ex: A commission was set up to investigate the accident.
commission.zh: 委員會（Workplace Relations Commission：勞資關係委員會）

committee.en: a group chosen to do a task
committee.ex: The committee will decide next week.

communication.en: sharing ideas and information with others
communication.ex: Good communication helps a team work well.

compensate.en: to make up for a loss or problem
compensate.ex: Nothing can compensate for the time we lost.

example.en: Hard work can compensate for a lack of talent.
example.zh: 努力可以彌補天分的不足。

note.meaning: 彌補損失或不足；也可指賠償。
note.usage: 常用 compensate for sth（彌補…）、compensate sb for sth（賠償某人…）。

noteEn.meaning: to make up for a loss or a lack of something.
noteEn.usage: Use "compensate for something" or "compensate someone for something".

noteEs.exampleTr: El trabajo duro puede compensar la falta de talento.
noteEs.meaning: compensar una pérdida o una falta; también indemnizar.
noteEs.usage: Se usa compensate for sth (compensar algo) y compensate sb for sth (indemnizar a alguien).

noteHi.exampleTr: मेहनत प्रतिभा की कमी की भरपाई कर सकती है।
noteHi.meaning: किसी नुक़सान या कमी की भरपाई करना; मुआवज़ा देना।
noteHi.usage: compensate for sth (भरपाई करना), compensate sb for sth (किसी को मुआवज़ा देना)।

noteJa.exampleTr: 努力は才能不足を補うことができる。
noteJa.meaning: 損失や不足を埋め合わせる。補償するという意味もある。
noteJa.usage: compensate for 〜（〜を補う）、compensate 人 for 〜（人に〜を補償する）の形で使う。

noteKo.exampleTr: 노력은 재능 부족을 메울 수 있다.
noteKo.meaning: 손실이나 부족을 메우다; 보상하다라는 뜻도 있다.
noteKo.usage: compensate for ~(~을 메우다), compensate 사람 for ~(사람에게 ~을 보상하다)로 쓴다.

concerned.ex: The book is concerned with family life.

conduct.ex: The police will conduct a full investigation.

conflict.ex: The conflict between the two neighbours lasted years.

confrontation.en: an angry fight or argument between sides
confrontation.ex: The protesters wanted to avoid a confrontation with police.

congress.en: Congress (part of a union body's name)

consequently.ex: It rained heavily; consequently, the match was cancelled.

consider.en: to think of something in a certain way
consider.ex: Many people consider him the best player.

contact.ex: I have had no contact with him for years.

contend.en: to argue that something is true
contend.ex: Critics contend that the plan is too expensive.

contingent.ex: The deal is contingent on government funding.

example.en: Our trip is contingent on the weather.
example.zh: 我們的旅行要看天氣而定。

note.meaning: 取決於某件尚未確定的事；要看…而定。
note.usage: 固定搭配 contingent on/upon sth，常見於正式寫作，可替代 depend on。

noteEn.meaning: depending on something that is not yet certain.
noteEn.usage: Always "contingent on/upon"; a formal way to say "depends on".

noteEs.meaning: que depende de algo que todavía no es seguro.
noteEs.usage: Se usa con contingent on/upon; es una forma formal de decir depend on.

noteHi.exampleTr: हमारी यात्रा मौसम पर निर्भर है।
noteHi.meaning: किसी ऐसी बात पर निर्भर जो अभी तय नहीं है।
noteHi.usage: हमेशा contingent on/upon के साथ; औपचारिक लेखन में depend on की जगह।

noteJa.exampleTr: 私たちの旅行は天気次第だ。
noteJa.meaning: まだ確定していない事柄に左右されること；〜次第である。
noteJa.usage: contingent on/upon の形で使う。depend on のフォーマルな言い換え。

noteKo.meaning: 아직 확정되지 않은 일에 달려 있는.
noteKo.usage: contingent on/upon 형태로 쓰며, depend on의 격식 있는 표현이다.

court.en: a place where legal cases are decided
court.ex: She works as a clerk at the local court.
court.zh: 法院（Labour Court：勞資法院；court staff：法院職員）

crucially.ex: Crucially, the new drug has very few side effects.
crucially.hi: सबसे अहम बात यह है कि

day.ex: It was a long day at work.

days.ex: We stayed there for three days.

deal.ex: The union and the company reached a deal.

delay.ex: The flight delay lasted two hours.

department.en: a part of a government or organisation
department.ex: He works in the health department.

development.en: a new event that changes a situation
development.ex: Police are watching the latest developments closely.

dialogue.ex: The leaders called for dialogue to end the war.

discussions.ex: Discussions about the new park continue.

dispute.ex: The pay dispute lasted three months.

disruption.en: problems that stop normal life or work
disruption.ex: The roadworks caused disruption for weeks.

distinct.ex: The two languages are quite distinct.

do.en: used instead of repeating a verb
do.ex: I like tea, and my sister does too.

down.ex: The talks broke down late on Monday.
down.hi: (stand down: वापस लेना; break down: टूटना)
down.ja: （stand down：取りやめる；break down：決裂する）

drew.ex: The concert drew a crowd of ten thousand.

due.en: expected or scheduled to happen at a certain time
due.ex: The report is due to be published next month.

earlier.ex: Earlier versions of the app were slower.

earmarked.en: set aside for a particular purpose
earmarked.ex: The money was earmarked for building new schools.
earmarked.ja: 〜に充てられた；〜用に指定された

endorsed.ex: The proposal was endorsed by the city council.

example.en: The board endorsed the new safety plan.
example.zh: 董事會正式批准了新的安全計畫。

note.meaning: 正式表示同意或支持某項決定、計畫或人選。
note.usage: 常用被動 be endorsed by + 機構；也可指名人代言產品。

noteEn.meaning: to officially approve or support a decision, plan or person.
noteEn.usage: Often passive: "be endorsed by" a group.

noteEs.exampleTr: La junta aprobó el nuevo plan de seguridad.
noteEs.meaning: aprobar o apoyar oficialmente una decisión, un plan o a una persona.
noteEs.usage: Es común en pasiva: be endorsed by + organismo; también se usa para famosos que promocionan productos.

noteHi.exampleTr: बोर्ड ने नई सुरक्षा योजना को मंज़ूरी दी।
noteHi.meaning: किसी निर्णय, योजना या व्यक्ति का आधिकारिक समर्थन या मंज़ूरी देना।
noteHi.usage: अक्सर passive: be endorsed by + संस्था; उत्पाद के प्रचार के लिए भी प्रयोग।

noteJa.exampleTr: 取締役会は新しい安全計画を承認した。
noteJa.meaning: 決定・計画・人物を公式に承認・支持すること。
noteJa.usage: 受動態 be endorsed by＋組織 の形が多い。有名人が商品を推薦する意味でも使う。

noteKo.meaning: 결정, 계획, 사람을 공식적으로 승인하거나 지지하다.
noteKo.usage: 수동태 be endorsed by + 기관 형태가 흔하며, 유명인의 상품 홍보에도 쓰인다.

enlisted.ex: We enlisted friends to help us move.

environment.en: the natural world of land, air and water
environment.zh: 環境（Department of the Environment：環境部）

eroded.ex: Rising prices have eroded our savings.

example.en: Years of scandal have eroded public trust in the bank.
example.zh: 多年的醜聞削弱了民眾對這家銀行的信任。

note.meaning: （價值、權力、信心等）被逐漸削弱或減少。
note.usage: 常用被動 be eroded by sth；如 inflation erodes wages（通膨侵蝕薪資）。

noteEn.meaning: to slowly make value, power or trust smaller or weaker.
noteEn.usage: Often passive: "be eroded by"; e.g. "inflation erodes wages".

noteEs.exampleTr: Años de escándalos han erosionado la confianza pública en el banco.
noteEs.meaning: reducir o debilitar poco a poco el valor, el poder o la confianza.
noteEs.usage: Se usa mucho en pasiva: be eroded by; por ejemplo, inflation erodes wages.

noteHi.exampleTr: वर्षों के घोटालों ने बैंक में जनता का भरोसा कमज़ोर कर दिया है।
noteHi.meaning: (मूल्य, शक्ति, भरोसा आदि का) धीरे-धीरे कम होना या कमज़ोर होना।
noteHi.usage: अक्सर passive: be eroded by; जैसे inflation erodes wages (महँगाई वेतन घटाती है)।

noteJa.exampleTr: 長年の不祥事でその銀行への国民の信頼は損なわれた。
noteJa.meaning: （価値・権力・信頼などを）少しずつ弱める、減らす。
noteJa.usage: 受動態 be eroded by がよく使われる。例：inflation erodes wages（インフレが賃金を目減りさせる）。

noteKo.exampleTr: 수년간의 스캔들이 그 은행에 대한 대중의 신뢰를 약화시켰다.
noteKo.meaning: (가치, 권력, 신뢰 등을) 조금씩 약화시키거나 줄이다.
noteKo.usage: 수동태 be eroded by로 자주 쓰인다. 예: inflation erodes wages(인플레이션이 임금을 잠식하다).

establish.en: to create or set up something lasting

exchanges.ex: There were angry exchanges between the two players.

exercise.en: an activity done for a purpose
exercise.ex: The survey is an annual exercise.

expected.ex: The new park is expected to open in May.
expected.ja: 予想された；見込まれる

exploratory.en: done to find out what is possible
exploratory.ex: The firms held exploratory talks about a merger.

fail.ex: Many new businesses fail in their first year.

failed.ex: The talks failed to produce a deal.

falls.en: falls short of: is less than
falls.ex: His score falls short of the top mark.

falter.en: to become weaker and start to fail
falter.ex: The economy began to falter last year.

faster.ex: Prices are rising faster than wages.

figures.ex: Several leading figures from sport attended the dinner.

first.en: coming before all others; for the first time, or at the beginning
first.ex: This is the first time I have visited Japan.

focused.en: giving attention to one clear aim
focused.ex: She is very focused on her exams.

followed.ex: A storm followed the hot weather.

follows.ex: The strike follows weeks of failed talks.

former.en: having been something in the past
former.ex: Kyoto is the former capital of Japan.

formerly.ex: The hotel was formerly a hospital.

fresh.ex: The coach brought fresh ideas to the team.

further.ex: Call us if you need further information.

furthermore.ex: The flat is cheap; furthermore, it is central.

general.en: (general secretary) the top officer of a group
general.ex: She was elected general secretary of the party.
general.zh: （general secretary：秘書長；secretary general：（部會）秘書長）

go.en: (go on strike) stop working as a protest
go.ex: The drivers may go on strike next month.
go.ja: （go on strike）ストライキを行う

gone.ex: The price of rice has gone up again.

government.en: the group that runs a country

groundwork.en: early work that prepares for later work
groundwork.ex: Good research lays the groundwork for a strong essay.

had.en: possessed; was involved (had a hand in)
had.ex: She had a key role in the project.

has.en: owns or holds; also forms perfect tense

have.ja: 持つ；〜しなければならない

head.ex: She is the head of the science department.

healthcare.ex: She wants a career in healthcare.

hold.en: (on hold) delayed or stopped for now
hold.ex: The building work is on hold until spring.

ictu.ja: ICTU（アイルランド労働組合会議）

ictu's.en: belonging to the Irish Congress of Trade Unions

if.en: used to talk about a condition

immediate.ex: There is no immediate danger to the public.

immediately.ex: Please call me immediately when you arrive.

impasse.en: a situation where no progress is possible
impasse.ex: The talks have reached an impasse.

example.en: The two sides finally broke the impasse after midnight.
example.zh: 雙方終於在午夜後打破了僵局。

note.meaning: 雙方無法達成共識、事情無法推進的僵局。
note.usage: 常用 reach an impasse（陷入僵局）、break the impasse（打破僵局）；正式用語。

noteEn.meaning: a situation where people cannot agree and nothing can move forward.
noteEn.usage: Common phrases: "reach an impasse" and "break the impasse".

noteEs.exampleTr: Las dos partes por fin rompieron el punto muerto pasada la medianoche.
noteEs.meaning: situación en la que no hay acuerdo y no se puede avanzar.
noteEs.usage: Se dice reach an impasse (llegar a un punto muerto) y break the impasse (desbloquearlo); es formal.

noteHi.exampleTr: दोनों पक्षों ने आख़िरकार आधी रात के बाद गतिरोध तोड़ा।
noteHi.meaning: ऐसी स्थिति जहाँ दोनों पक्ष सहमत नहीं होते और प्रगति रुक जाती है; गतिरोध।
noteHi.usage: reach an impasse (गतिरोध में फँसना), break the impasse (गतिरोध तोड़ना); औपचारिक शब्द।

noteJa.exampleTr: 両者は真夜中過ぎにようやく行き詰まりを打開した。
noteJa.meaning: 合意できず、物事が先に進まない行き詰まりの状態。
noteJa.usage: reach an impasse（行き詰まる）、break the impasse（打開する）の形で使う。硬い語。

noteKo.exampleTr: 양측은 자정이 넘어서야 마침내 교착 상태를 깼다.
noteKo.meaning: 합의가 되지 않아 일이 진척되지 않는 교착 상태.
noteKo.usage: reach an impasse(교착 상태에 빠지다), break the impasse(교착 상태를 깨다)로 쓰는 격식어.

example.en: The old school building is inadequate for 900 students.
example.zh: 那棟舊校舍容納不了九百名學生。

note.meaning: 不夠多或不夠好，無法滿足需要。
note.usage: 常用 inadequate for/to do；語氣比 not enough 正式，可加 wholly / totally 加強。

noteEn.meaning: not enough, or not good enough, for what is needed.
noteEn.usage: Use "inadequate for" or "inadequate to do"; it is more formal than "not enough".

noteEs.exampleTr: El viejo edificio escolar es insuficiente para 900 alumnos.
noteEs.meaning: que no es suficiente o no es lo bastante bueno para lo que se necesita.
noteEs.usage: Se usa inadequate for / to do; es más formal que not enough y se refuerza con wholly o totally.

noteHi.exampleTr: पुरानी स्कूल इमारत 900 छात्रों के लिए अपर्याप्त है।
noteHi.meaning: ज़रूरत पूरी करने के लिए पर्याप्त या अच्छा नहीं।
noteHi.usage: inadequate for / to do; यह not enough से अधिक औपचारिक है, wholly से ज़ोर दिया जा सकता है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 古い校舎は900人の生徒には不十分だ。
noteJa.meaning: 必要を満たすには量や質が足りないこと。
noteJa.usage: inadequate for / to do の形で使う。not enough より硬い表現で、wholly などで強調できる。

noteKo.usage: inadequate for / to do 형태로 쓰며, not enough보다 격식 있는 표현이다. wholly 등으로 강조한다.

increases.ex: There was a sharp increase in prices.

indicates.ex: The test indicates that the water is safe.

individuals.ex: Ten individuals signed up for the course.

industrial.es: laboral (industrial action: medidas de presión laboral)
industrial.ex: The union is planning industrial action over pay.
industrial.zh: 勞資的（industrial action：勞工抗爭行動）

inflation.ex: Inflation makes everyday goods more expensive.

insufficient.ex: There was insufficient time to finish.

intensive.en: involving a lot of effort in a short time
intensive.ex: She took an intensive English course.

involved.en: included; had as people taking part
involved.ex: The project involved over fifty volunteers.

joined.ex: She joined the club last year.

keen.en: wanting very much to do something
keen.ex: She is keen to learn the guitar.

keep.en: to continue to have or do something
keep.ex: He wants to keep his job after the operation.

kept.en: (keep up with) rise at the same speed as
kept.es: (kept up with) siguieron el ritmo de
kept.ex: Salaries have not kept up with house prices.

labour.en: work and workers (Labour Court: court for work disputes)
labour.ex: Labour officials met business leaders on Tuesday.
labour.zh: 勞工；勞資（Labour Court：勞資法院）

last.en: the one before this one (e.g. last year)
last.ex: We went to Japan last summer.

lay.en: to put in place; to prepare
lay.ex: The meeting will lay the foundations for a new plan.

lead.ex: She will lead the team next season.

leader.en: the person in charge of a group
leader.ex: The team leader called a short meeting.

least.ex: You should sleep at least seven hours a night.

lies.ex: The answer lies in hard work.
lies.zh: 在於（lie at the crux of：是…的核心）

made.ex: The coach made it clear that nobody was safe.

maintain.en: to keep saying something is true
maintain.ex: He maintains that he did nothing wrong.

many.ex: Many people work from home now.

meeting.en: an event where people gather to talk

met.ex: The club members met on Monday evening.

ministers.ex: The ministers met to discuss the budget.

mutual.en: felt or shared by both sides
mutual.ex: The two leaders have great mutual respect.

national.ex: The national team won the match.

nationwide.ex: There was a nationwide search for the missing boy.

paragraphs: A second big strike in Ireland will not happen next week. Public sector workers planned to stop work on Wednesday, 21 October. Now the unions have called it off.
On Friday, the Government and the unions agreed to start talks. The talks will begin at once. Three people will lead them.
One is Owen Reidy, a union leader. Another is Oonagh Buckley, a top official in a government department. The third is Kevin Foley. He is the head of the Workplace Relations Commission.
The workers want more pay. They say prices have gone up faster than their wages. The old pay deal ended in June.
More than 300,000 workers went on strike on 14 October. Teachers, nurses and many other workers took part.
The strike is only on hold. It could still happen if the talks fail.

Public sector workers in Ireland will not go on strike next Wednesday, 21 October. On Friday, the unions agreed to put the second strike on hold after the Government offered a new way to start talks about pay.

The Government said it would begin a short and intensive process with the unions. The aim is to agree on a basis for formal negotiations on a new pay deal. These negotiations would take place at the Workplace Relations Commission (WRC). The talks are expected to start immediately.

Three people will lead the process. Owen Reidy is the general secretary of the Irish Congress of Trade Unions (ICTU). Oonagh Buckley is a senior official at the Department of the Environment. Kevin Foley is the head of the WRC and used to lead the Labour Court.
The decision came after the public services committee of ICTU met on Friday afternoon. In the days before, the two sides had been talking quietly in private.

More than 300,000 workers, including teachers, healthcare staff and court employees, took part in the first strike on 14 October. The unions say wages have not kept up with rising prices since the last pay agreement ended in June. The Government set aside €1.2 billion for pay in the budget, but the unions say this is not enough.
The strike has been suspended, not cancelled. If the talks do not succeed, workers could still walk out again.
A second nationwide public sector strike, planned for next Wednesday, 21 October, has been suspended after unions and the Government agreed on a route towards talks on a new pay deal.

In a statement on Friday, the Government said it had appointed three people to run a 'focused and intensive exercise' with the unions. Its purpose is to establish a basis for formal negotiations at the Workplace Relations Commission (WRC). The process is expected to begin straight away.

The trio are Owen Reidy, general secretary of the Irish Congress of Trade Unions (ICTU); Oonagh Buckley, secretary general of the Department of the Environment; and Kevin Foley, chairperson of the WRC and a former chair of the Labour Court.

ICTU, the umbrella body for trade unions, agreed to the suspension after its public services committee met on Friday afternoon. The breakthrough followed several days of behind-the-scenes contact between the two sides.

The dispute centres on pay. The previous public sector agreement expired in June, and unions argue that earlier increases have failed to keep pace with inflation. They also say the €1.2 billion allocated for public pay in the budget falls well short. More than 300,000 workers, from nurses to teachers, joined the first stoppage on 14 October.
Union leaders have made clear that the action has been paused rather than abandoned, so further strikes remain possible if the preliminary talks break down.

The threat of a second day of disruption across Ireland's public services has receded, after unions agreed to stand down a strike scheduled for Wednesday, 21 October, in return for a fresh attempt at dialogue with the Government.

Ministers announced on Friday that they had enlisted three figures to oversee what they termed a focused and intensive exercise. Its remit is to lay the groundwork for formal pay negotiations under the auspices of the Workplace Relations Commission (WRC), and discussions are due to commence without delay.

The appointees bring a blend of perspectives: Owen Reidy, general secretary of the Irish Congress of Trade Unions (ICTU); Oonagh Buckley, secretary general of the Department of the Environment; and Kevin Foley, who chairs the WRC and previously presided over the Labour Court.

The climbdown was sanctioned by ICTU's public services committee at a meeting on Friday afternoon. It was preceded by days of discreet back-channel exchanges, suggesting that both camps were keen to avoid a protracted confrontation.

At the root of the impasse lies pay. The last national agreement lapsed in June, and unions contend that previous rises have been eroded by inflation. They regard the €1.2 billion earmarked in the budget as wholly inadequate. The first walkout, on 14 October, drew more than 300,000 workers, among them nurses, teachers and court staff.
Crucially, the strike has merely been suspended. Should the exploratory talks falter, unions retain the option of resuming industrial action.

A second national strike by public sector workers in Ireland, which had been scheduled for Wednesday, 21 October, has been suspended. Consequently, the immediate prospect of widespread disruption to public services has been averted, at least temporarily.

This development follows an announcement by the Government that three individuals have been appointed to conduct a focused and intensive process with the unions. The principal objective is to establish a substantial basis for formal negotiations on a new pay agreement, which would subsequently take place at the Workplace Relations Commission (WRC). The process is expected to commence immediately.

The three appointees represent distinct institutional perspectives: Owen Reidy, general secretary of the Irish Congress of Trade Unions (ICTU); Oonagh Buckley, secretary general of the Department of the Environment; and Kevin Foley, chairperson of the WRC and formerly chair of the Labour Court.

The decision to suspend the action was endorsed by ICTU's public services committee on Friday afternoon. Notably, it was preceded by several days of confidential communication between the parties, which indicates a mutual reluctance to prolong the conflict.

The dispute is fundamentally concerned with remuneration. The previous agreement expired in June, and the unions maintain that earlier increases have been insufficient to compensate for inflation. Furthermore, they consider the €1.2 billion allocated in the budget to be inadequate. The first stoppage, on 14 October, involved more than 300,000 employees, including nurses, teachers and court staff.
Nevertheless, it should be emphasised that the strike has been suspended rather than cancelled. Whether it is ultimately abandoned is therefore contingent upon the outcome of the preliminary talks.
